- Rate limits and burst behavior during traffic spikes (you mentioned holiday-level burst patterns).
- Error budget handling and reporting (how retries, degradations, and fallbacks count toward the budget).
- Failover behavior: what happens during regional outage (model compatibility, stateful sessions/streams).

What we'll send you by EOD Monday
- Short SLO comparison doc (Redwood vs. typical hyperscaler managed endpoints) with uptime, p95/p99 latencies, and error-budget math.
- Sample logs and a short log-format spec so your infra team can validate observability ingestion.
- Suggested test harness and a proposed set of smoke/load tests (high-QPS sustained, burst, and long-lived streams).

Suggested next steps
1) I'll share the SLO comparison and a couple attachments (log sample + XLS) — please share with your platform team.
2) If the numbers look good, propose a 60–90 minute technical validation call with your infra and our SREs next week to kick off the tests.
3) We can scope a short POC (2–4 weeks) to run the test harness if you want empirical numbers.

Can you confirm whether your procurement/legal team needs a draft SLA/contract language up front, or if you'd prefer to wait until after the POC?

Thanks — Ben

Appreciate the recap and quick turnaround. A few clarifying items from my side before we bring our infra folks in: 

1) Rate limits: can you confirm per-API-key and per-tenant rate limits for the hosted API? For our use case we need predictable per-tenant ingress (we often have a single API key shared across many internal services).
2) Streams: how are long-lived streaming requests treated for SLOs and error budgets? Do they count as a single request for rate-limiting and error-budget purposes or by bytes/tokens?
3) SLA language: yes, please share a draft. Our legal team typically wants explicit monthly uptime % and error-budget treatment for retries and fallback behavior.
4) Would appreciate an explicit failover description (automatic regional failover vs. async replay) and whether session affinity/stateful KV caches survive a failover.

Also — can you share the proposed test scenarios and a simple DocuSign/contract clip if you're comfortable? That'll speed procurement if we line up the POC.

Jessica —

Looping in Marissa (SRE/solutions) and Rishi (product infra) to answer the technical specifics. Per your notes: we will include a draft SLA and explicit failover behavior in the attachment.

Proposed quick answers so you have something to review ahead of the SRE call: 
- Per-tenant rate limits: Hosted API default is 500 requests/sec per tenant with configurable dedicated capacity options for higher sustained throughput (Dedicated customers routinely run several thousand rps).
- Burst policies allow up to ~2k rps for short windows; we can document exact token-bucket params.
- Streaming: long-lived streams count as active sessions for rate-limiting; error-budget accounting treats a stream failure as a single failure event but we also report partial output and byte/token counts in the logs. We'll provide clear language so it matches procurement expectations.
- Failover: Redwood supports cross-region failover with graceful degradation — KV cache is best-effort to replicate; session affinity is sticky within a region, and failover will route to the next healthy region with possible cold-starts for KV caches.

Marissa / Rishi — can you attach the SLO comparison table and the sample logs? Also, any tweaks to the numbers above?

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Hi Jessica —

Thanks for the questions. Attaching a short XLS that shows Redwood vs two typical hyperscaler-managed endpoints (summary row at top). Key points pulled out below for quick reference: 

SLA / uptime
- Redwood Hosted: 99.95% monthly uptime SLA (standard).
- Redwood Dedicated: can be contractually set to 99.99% with reserved pools and multi-zone redundancy.
- Hyperscaler baseline offerings we see: often 99.9% for managed endpoints unless you buy dedicated infra.

Error budget & incident accounting
- 99.95% => ~22 minutes/month error budget. We count service-level failures (5xx/error responses) toward the budget. Client-side retries with exponential backoff are not charged to the budget unless server returns repeated 5xx for the retried requests.
- For streams: a stream disconnect that results in incomplete output is recorded as a single failure for budget accounting; we include token-level metrics in the exported logs so you can roll your own counting if desired.

Rate limiting & burst behavior
- Hosted default: 500 rps per tenant, token-bucket burst up to 2k for short windows (subject to fair-use).
- Dedicated: configurable; typical committed throughput options (example: 2k/5k/10k rps) with predictable tail latency SLAs.

Failover behavior
- Automatic multi-region routing: Redwood routes to healthy regions according to customer routing policy. In the event of region outage, requests are retried to the next region per policy.
- KV cache and session affinity: KV caches are cached locally per serving node; we provide async warm-up and cache prefill options for Dedicated deployments. Stateful sessions may see cold-start latency after failover — we itemize this in the SLA appendix.

Observability & reporting
- We provide per-tenant token-level logs, p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, and a weekly SLA report. Real-time alerts and an incident postmortem are provided for Sev1 events.

Suggested test matrix (what we can run with you)
- Sustained load: 1000 rps sustained for 1 hour (Hosted) and report p99 latency and error rate.
- Burst test: 2k rps sustained for 5 minutes from multiple regions.
- Streams: 200 concurrent long-lived streams for 30 minutes, validate reconnection behavior and final output fidelity.
- Failover drill: simulate regional outage and measure cold-start latency impact on session-affine requests.

Attachments included: redwood-slo-comparison-table.xlsx; slo-diagrams.pdf; log-sample-20260315.txt

If these numbers align with your expectations, let's schedule the technical validation call next Wednesday at 2pm PT (Ben — can you confirm?). We'll bring our SRE and product infra to run through test requirements and data access.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
